Hyperkalemia is a potential risk, especially when trimethoprim is administered at high doses, in patients with renal insufficiency, or when combined with other medications that elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which can exacerbate hyperkalemia. Potassium citrate also increases serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels of pralatrexate by reducing its renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Sulfamethoxazole can elevate the levels or effects of procainamide due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Similarly, procainamide can increase the levels or effects of trimethoprim through the same mechanism. Monitoring is necessary. 4. Both prochlorperazine and sulfamethoxazole, as well as prochlorperazine and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 5. Promazine, when combined with sulfamethoxazole or trimethoprim, can increase the QTc interval. Additionally, promazine may enhance the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to increased myelosuppression. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Promethazine, when used with trimethoprim or sulfamethoxazole, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Protriptyline, when combined with sulfamethoxazole or trimethoprim, can increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 8. Trimethoprim and quinapril both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 9. Quinidine can increase the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance. Monitoring is recommended. 10. Ramipril and trimethoprim both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is advised. 11. Sulfamethoxazole and ranolazine, as well as ranolazine and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 12. Trimethoprim increases the levels of repaglinide by reducing its metabolism. Sulfamethoxazole increases repaglinide levels through plasma protein binding competition. Monitoring is required. 13. Trimethoprim can increase the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting CYP2C8 metabolism. Dose reduction of resmetirom is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 14. Sulfamethoxazole and risperidone, as well as risperidone and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised. 15. Rifabutin and rifampin can decrease the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 16. Sacubitril/valsartan and trimethoprim both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 17. Trimethoprim can increase the levels or effects of selexipag by reducing its metabolism. Dose reduction of selexipag to once daily is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 18. Trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole can reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics may reduce efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Monitoring is advised. 19. Sparsentan can decrease the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Sparsentan reduces the efficacy of CYP2C9 substrates. Monitoring is recommended. 20. Trimethoprim and spironolactone both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 21. Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised. 22. Tecovirimat can decrease the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitoring of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is recommended. 23. Telavancin and trimethoprim, as well as sulfamethoxazole and telavancin, can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is necessary. 24. Trimethoprim and telmisartan both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 25. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Thioridazine and sulfamethoxazole, as well as thioridazine and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 27. Trimethoprim and trandolapril both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 28. Trazodone and sulfamethoxazole, as well as trazodone and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Trimethoprim and triamterene both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 30. Trifluoperazine and sulfamethoxazole, as well as trifluoperazine and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 31. Trimipramine and trimethoprim, as well as trimipramine and sulfamethoxazole, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Trimethoprim and tropisetron, as well as sulfamethoxazole and tropisetron, can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised. 33. Sulfamethoxazole and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase hepatotoxicity risk when combined. Close monitoring of liver enzymes and consideration of alternative medications are recommended. 34. Valsartan and trimethoprim both elevate serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia, particularly in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Monitoring is essential. 35. Sulfamethoxazole and venlafaxine, as well as trimethoprim and venlafaxine, can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised. 36. Voclosporin and trimethoprim both decrease serum potassium levels. Monitoring is recommended. 37. Sulfamethoxazole and voriconazole, as well as trimethoprim and voriconazole, can prolong the QTc interval. Monitoring is advised. 38. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism and through protein-binding displacement. A 10-20% reduction in warfarin dose may be necessary. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 39. Trimethoprim increases the levels of zidovudine by reducing its renal clearance, potentially increasing toxicity. Monitoring is recommended. 40. Sulfamethoxazole and ziprasidone, as well as trimethoprim and ziprasidone, can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 41. Acetazolamide can increase the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 42. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Amiloride and trimethoprim, as well as amiloride and sulfamethoxazole, may interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Sulfamethoxazole interferes with the chemical color development of aminohippurate (PAH), which is essential for accurate renal clearance analysis. 45. Anastrozole can increase the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 46. Amiodarone can increase the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of amitriptyline through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 48. Amobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of amoxapine through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 50. Aspirin rectal increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 51. Sulfamethoxazole and azathioprine may cause leukopenia due to additive myelosuppression. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Azithromycin and sulfamethoxazole, as well as azithromycin and trimethoprim, can prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole can reduce the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 54. Bendroflumethiazide and trimethoprim, as well as bendroflumethiazide and sulfamethoxazole, may interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Trimethoprim can decrease the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 56. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of bosentan by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Chlorothiazide and trimethoprim, as well as chlorothiazide and sulfamethoxazole, may interact through an unspecified mechanism, increasing the risk of hyponatremia. The clinical significance is unknown. 58. Bumetanide increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 59. Butabarbital and butalbital can decrease the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Carbamazepine can decrease the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 61. Sulfamethoxazole can increase the levels or effects of celecoxib by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 62. Chlorthalidone and trimethoprim, as well as chlorthalidone and sulfamethoxazole, may interact through an unspecified mechanism, increasing the risk of hyponatremia. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Choline magnesium trisalicylate increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 64. Cyclopenthiazide and trimethoprim, as well as cyclopenthiazide and sulfamethoxazole, may interact through an unspecified mechanism, increasing the risk of hyponatremia. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Cimetidine can increase the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 66. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of clomipramine through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 67. Cyclophosphamide can increase the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 68. Danazol can increase the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 69. Sulfamethoxazole and dapsone, as well as trimethoprim and dapsone, can increase each other's levels by reducing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. 70. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of desipramine through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown.
